chunks: Sa'd narrated from Abu Ja'far, from al-Barqi, from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Nawfali, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah or someone else who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him, 'Should I separate the Witr [prayer]?' He said, 'Yes.' I asked him, 'Sometimes I get thirsty, so should I drink water?' He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْوَتْر: Witr, the odd-numbered prayer offered at night, often concluding the night prayer

ai.seo_question: Can I break my night prayer to drink water if I get thirsty?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the permissibility of breaking the Witr prayer to drink water is confirmed, highlighting the practical flexibility (rukhas) granted in night prayers to accommodate physical needs without invalidating the act of worship. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that Witr, while highly recommended, retains the status of a valid prayer where minor interruptions for necessity do not nullify its continuity. The hadith underscores the balance between spiritual devotion and bodily comfort, a key theme in the detailed rulings of Salat al-Layl found in works like Tahdhib al-Ahkam.
